body:
Steps to reproduce locally / on a dev-server:
1) It's required to force restore procedure to increase schema version. The easiest way to do that is to backup with one partitioning version and restore to the cluster with increased partitioning version -- this is a real scenario for upgrades from version < 2.15.1.0-b122 to the version >= 2.15.1.0-b122
```
$ ./bin/yb-ctl start --master_flags "TEST_partitioning_version=0" \
  --tserver_flags "TEST_partitioning_version=0"
```
2) Create a table
```
$ ./bin/ysqlsh -c "create table t1(id int primary key, name text)"
$ ./bin/ysqlsh -c "insert into t1 select i, i::text from generate_series(1,50000) as i"
```
3) Make a backup
```
$ rm -rf ~/tmp/backup_test; mkdir ~/tmp/backup_test
$ source ~/code/yugabyte-db/build/venv/bin/activate
$ ./managed/devops/bin/yb_backup.py --masters 127.0.0.1 \
--remote_yb_admin_binary ./build/latest/bin/yb-admin \
--remote_ysql_dump_binary ./build/latest/postgres/bin/ysql_dump \
--remote_ysql_shell_binary ./build/latest/postgres/bin/ysqlsh --no_ssh \
--storage_type nfs --nfs_storage_path ~/yugabyte-data \
--backup_location ~/tmp/backup_test --no_auto_name \
--keyspace ysql.yugabyte create
```
4) Recreate cluster with partitioning_version greater previous value (starting from 2.15.1.0-b122 default value is 1)
```
$ ./bin/yb-ctl destroy && ./bin/yb-ctl start
```
5) Restore previous backup
```
$ ./managed/devops/bin/yb_backup.py --masters 127.0.0.1 \
--remote_yb_admin_binary ./build/latest/bin/yb-admin \
--remote_ysql_dump_binary ./build/latest/postgres/bin/ysql_dump \
--remote_ysql_shell_binary ./build/latest/postgres/bin/ysqlsh --no_ssh \
--storage_type nfs --nfs_storage_path ~/yugabyte-data \
--backup_location ~/tmp/backup_test --no_auto_name \
--keyspace ysql.yugabyte restore
```
6) Start `./bin/ysqlsh` and execute the following commands
```
BEGIN TRANSACTION; SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ;
select count(*) from t1;
````
7) The following error appears:
```
ERROR:  Query error: schema version mismatch for table 000033e8000030008000000000004000: expected 1, got 0
```
8) Abort transaction and try again, the same error appears:
```
ABORT TRANSACTION;
BEGIN TRANSACTION; SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ;
select count(*) from t1;
ABORT TRANSACTION;
```
9) To resolve the error any select request should be done without transaction:
```
select * from t1 limit 1;
```
10) Try select within transaction once again, now it works:
```
BEGIN TRANSACTION; SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ;
select count(*) from t1;
ABORT TRANSACTION;
```
11) Steps 6-10 may require two parallel shells, but I was able to reproduce with a single shell on a dev-server

Quick RCA: this is happening because PG's table cache entry is not invalidated for "transaction blocks", refer to this [code](https://github.com/yugabyte/yugabyte-db/blob/4e74c5991925f2604e11f6c49127cd4ad6dfc7b3/src/postgres/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L3831) for the details

More details:
1) Restoration is happening in three main steps:
a) DDL is restored from YSQLDump
b) Tables structure is adjusted in accordance with backuped tablets structure (partitioning, columns, etc)
c) Data is restored
2) Schema can be changed on the step 1.a currently for two cases only:
a) Columns ids was changed and should be restored, [code link](https://github.com/yugabyte/yugabyte-db/blob/4e74c5991925f2604e11f6c49127cd4ad6dfc7b3/ent/src/yb/master/catalog_manager_ent.cc#L1808)
b) Partitioning version was changed and the original one should be restored, [code link](https://github.com/yugabyte/yugabyte-db/blob/4e74c5991925f2604e11f6c49127cd4ad6dfc7b3/ent/src/yb/master/catalog_manager_ent.cc#L1843)
3) Looks like the test is rather straightforward and the case 2.a is never hit, but actually we will face exactly the same error if that will happen
4) The case 2.b is hit because partitioning version was changed with this commit globally; above are the steps how to reproduce for every build / commit starting from 2.15.1.0-b122 / 61985b6e0cf2ebbcab943c66ddda8138c0075dc1
5) PG detects the schema version has been changed, but due to the current design does not invalidates table entry in the cache when this's happening in a transactional block, [code link](https://github.com/yugabyte/yugabyte-db/blob/4e74c5991925f2604e11f6c49127cd4ad6dfc7b3/src/postgres/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L3838)
6) For the non-transactional queries PG invalidates table entry in the cache and re-sends the request by itself, [code link](https://github.com/yugabyte/yugabyte-db/blob/4e74c5991925f2604e11f6c49127cd4ad6dfc7b3/src/postgres/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L3874), this can be confirmed with a log (added more traces, starting with `AR-`), at least message about invalidation will be observed:
```
[ts-1] I0707 08:33:31.971633 24253 tablet.cc:1507] AR-HandlePgsqlReadRequest:
       table = 000033e5000030008000000000004100,
       table_info::schema_version = 1, read_requst::schema_version = 0
[ts-1] E0707 08:33:31.971715 24253 tablet.cc:1518] AR-HandlePgsqlReadRequest:
       table = 000033e5000030008000000000004100 schema version mismatch! expected = 1, got = 0
[ts-1] 2022-07-07 08:33:31.976 UTC [24497] LOG:  
       invalidating table cache entry 000033e5000030008000000000004100
[ts-1] I0707 08:33:31.996312 24252 tablet.cc:1507] AR-HandlePgsqlReadRequest:
       table = 000033e5000030008000000000004100,
       table_info::schema_version = 1, read_requst::schema_version = 1
```

Having all of this, what is observed in the test is the expected behaviour in accordance with current design.
Possible solutions:
1) Do not update schema version for partitioning_version change during restore -- not OK, possible may lead to a situation that other masters/tservers won't get up-to-date info in time; also this does not solve the case for changing columns ids during restoration. By the way, two schema's having difference only in partitioning_version are considered equal (partitioning_version is ignored during comparison).
2) Force restore procedure to make PG invalidate it's cache. Looks like it should be done for all connections (having several ybsqlsh opened, a non-transactional select or reconnect is required for all shells), but not 100% sure
3) After restore is done a simple non-transactional select can be done to force to update table entry in the cache thus getting the latest version.
4) Maybe (3) should be taken into account for designed apps, tests an so on -- transactional request may fail right after restore and the app or test should force a simple request to invalidate the cache.

cc @bmatican @m-iancu to identify next steps.

I’ve made additional testing related to the time of executing ysqlsh with subsequent “begin transaction + select” statements:

- executed `ysqlsh` before restore and kept open during restore
- executed `ysqlsh` right after the restore had been finished
- executed `ysqlsh` in ~90 seconds after the restore had been finished
- executed `ysqlsh` in ~315 seconds after the restore had been finished
- executed `ysqlsh` in ~615 seconds after the restore had been finished
- executed `ysqlsh` twice right after restore, the first time run `\d` only, second time - the same “begin transaction + select” statements

Every time I got `ERROR: Query error: schema version mismatch for table <uuid>: expected 1, got 0`. But the subsequent quit and then starting `ysqlsh` with “begin transaction + select” statement works fine. So, the cache got updated during the second connection (or on first connection termination?) when the first connection had the error.
As of now it looks like an internal PG cache was not updated for any reason on the first connection after the restore had been finished.

One important thing, `ysqlsh -f YSQLDump` is called during restore procedure to exec DDL, and maybe at this step something got cached without handling subsequent schema updates which are happening in  `CatalogManager::ImportTableEntry()` at [this](https://github.com/yugabyte/yugabyte-db/blob/44a35b99ac0641ad3106a9ba42ee91b30c91101d/ent/src/yb/master/catalog_manager_ent.cc#L1837), [this](https://github.com/yugabyte/yugabyte-db/blob/44a35b99ac0641ad3106a9ba42ee91b30c91101d/ent/src/yb/master/catalog_manager_ent.cc#L1852) and [this](https://github.com/yugabyte/yugabyte-db/blob/44a35b99ac0641ad3106a9ba42ee91b30c91101d/ent/src/yb/master/catalog_manager_ent.cc#L1859) lines.

postgres log content during the time of restoration looks more or less is expected (ERROR for database is expected)
```
I0707 16:41:13.667217 7608 mem_tracker.cc:299] MemTracker: hard memory limit is 9.441395 GB
I0707 16:41:13.667376 7608 mem_tracker.cc:301] MemTracker: soft memory limit is 8.025186 GB

I0707 16:41:18.349052 7623 mem_tracker.cc:299] MemTracker: hard memory limit is 9.441395 GB

```

In case of cache refresh postgres invalidates its table cache (and table cache in `PgClientService` as well). Here is the stack trace for such invalidation

```
@     0x7f0457df7a24  yb::pggate::PgSession::InvalidateAllTablesCache() (src/yb/yql/pggate/pg_session.cc:468)

@           0xacd86c  YBRefreshCache (src/postgres/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c:3748)
@           0xace681  YBCheckSharedCatalogCacheVersion (src/postgres/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c:4045)
@           0xac94d6  PostgresMain (src/postgres/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c:5197)
@           0x9fdd4c  BackendRun (src/postgres/src/backend/postmaster/postmaster.c:4560)
@           0x9fce44  BackendStartup (src/postgres/src/backend/postmaster/postmaster.c:4198)
@           0x9fbaaa  ServerLoop (src/postgres/src/backend/postmaster/postmaster.c:1767)
@           0x9f8eb7  PostmasterMain (src/postgres/src/backend/postmaster/postmaster.c:1423)
@           0x904ee7  PostgresServerProcessMain (src/postgres/src/backend/main/main.c:234)
@           0x905311 
@     0x7f04572f8cf2 
@           0x551a6d 
```

As a result current problem can be fixed by changing postgre's sys catalog version after restore procedure.

issue.title: [DocDB] YBOperation.partition_key encoding should respect null value

repository.name: yugabyte-db
repository.description: YugabyteDB - the cloud native distributed SQL database for mission-critical applications.

issue.body:
Jira Link: [[DB-363]](https://yugabyte.atlassian.net/browse/DB-363)
### Description

Let's assume the following example
```
# create table test1(id int primary key, name text);
# create unique index idx1 on test1(name ASC) split at values(('p'));
# insert into test1 values(3, 'p');
```
and encoded partition bound looks like `5370000021` in hex

In accordance with [documentation](https://github.com/yugabyte/yugabyte-db/blob/c2deaf4af152b08e009f945ca7d662d325d6c46a/src/yb/common/pg_system_attr.h#L38) column `ybuniqueidxkeysuffix` may be of `kNullLow`, `kNullHigh` or `base table ctid` values. Hence the following possible `YBOperation.partition_key` should be concerned as correctly encoded values (in hex):
```
537000002421 > 5370000021
537000007C21 > 5370000021
537000005347C0C4488000010001022121000021> 5370000021
```

In all of these cases the write operation will be forwarded to a correct tablet as all possible values for the first byte are greater than the encoded value of `kGroupEnd == 0x21`.
But as of now, first and second options are encoded with `537000000021` < `5370000021`. Mainly, this is happening because `QLValuePB::VALUE_NOT_SET` is treated as `kLowest` for a `YBOperation.partition_key`, but should not. There is a stack of calls that leads to the inconsistency:
[GetRangeComponents()](https://github.com/yugabyte/yugabyte-db/blob/8a285058e7edea3d1510f058c199db5479c7d238/src/yb/client/yb_op.cc#L303)
[GetRangePartitionKey()](https://github.com/yugabyte/yugabyte-db/blob/8a285058e7edea3d1510f058c199db5479c7d238/src/yb/client/yb_op.cc#L329)
[InitWritePartitionKey()](https://github.com/yugabyte/yugabyte-db/blob/8a285058e7edea3d1510f058c199db5479c7d238/src/yb/client/yb_op.cc#L370)

The fact the `YBOperation.partition_key` has incorrect format is also confirmed by a manual decoding (via unit test), the following error appears:
```Error when decoding range components of a document key: Expected a primitive value type, got kLowest.```

*Note*. Refer to [KeyEntryValue::NullValue()](https://github.com/yugabyte/yugabyte-db/blob/c2deaf4af152b08e009f945ca7d662d325d6c46a/src/yb/docdb/primitive_value.cc#L1532) and PostgreSQL [documentation](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/queries-order.html) for details on how null should be encoded. By default NULL LAST approach is used or ASC ordering and NULL FIRST for DESC ordering.

*Step to reproduce the issue:*

1. Create a cluster with `enable_automatic_tablet_splitting=true`:
```
./bin/yb-ctl create --master_flags="enable_automatic_tablet_splitting=true,tablet_split_low_phase_shard_count_per_node=16,tablet_split_low_phase_size_threshold_bytes=13421" --tserver_flags="yb_num_shards_per_tserver=1"
```
2. Create a table and a unique index
```
# create table test1(id int primary key, name text);
# create unique index idx1 on test1(name ASC) split at values(('p'));
```
Tablets info after statements have been executed:
```
yugabyte        idx1       000033e1000030008000000000004005        d75c1be78e94456d9803758d6650a897        range: [<start>, DocKey([], ["p"]))
yugabyte        idx1       000033e1000030008000000000004005        b5531d9aa54a45fb821fcf2baca3f268        range: [DocKey([], ["p"]), <end>)
```
3. Insert a row with a value that matches partition bounds
```
# insert into test1 values(3, 'p');
```
YBOperation is forwarded to the first tablet `d75c1be78e94456d9803758d6650a897` as `YBOperation.partition_key` is less than the second partition lower bound: `537000000021` < `5370000021`. But the operation should have been forwarded to the second tablet in accordance with range bounds. Tablets dump confirms the inserted row is persisted in the first tablet (with respect to DocDB format):
```
tablet-d75c1be78e94456d9803758d6650a897 in readable format:
SubDocKey(DocKey([], ["p", null]), [SystemColumnId(0); HT{ physical: 1649185585666746 }]) -> null; intent doc ht: HT{ physical: 1649185585665110 }
SubDocKey(DocKey([], ["p", null]), [ColumnId(12); HT{ physical: 1649185585666746 w: 1 }]) -> "G\xfc\xa0H\x80\x00\x00\x03!!"; intent doc ht: HT{ physical: 1649185585665110 w: 1 }

Data Block # 1 @ 0051
--------------------------------------
  HEX    5370000024214A80238001785106292545804A: 238001785106292BA9804A24
  ASCII  S p : # Ä  x Q  ) + © Ä J $ 
  ------
  HEX    5370000024214B8C238001785106292545803FAB: 238001785106292BA9803FAB5347FCA048800000032121
  ASCII  S p : # Ä  x Q  ) + © Ä ? ´ S G ¸ † H Ä 
  ------

tablet-b5531d9aa54a45fb821fcf2baca3f268
<empty>
```

[DB-363]: https://yugabyte.atlassian.net/browse/DB-363?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ
